evals.expected_output: Answers from Table 9-12 (Wk07 Ch11 p16): 3-6 sets, 6-12 reps, 30-90s rest, 67-85% 1RM. Cites the lesson/page. Does not invent numbers. May add the Resistance FITT-VP context (Table 11-10) with a citation.
expectations: States the hypertrophy set range as 3-6 sets
States the hypertrophy rep range as 6-12 reps
States the hypertrophy rest interval as 30-90 seconds
States the hypertrophy intensity as 67-85% 1RM
Cites a specific course location for the numbers (e.g. Table 9-12, or Week 07 / Ch 11 / page 16)
Does not attribute to the course any hypertrophy set/rep/rest/intensity number that conflicts with Table 9-12
Ties the numbers to the user's own course material rather than presenting them only as generic industry hypertrophy guidelines

evals.prompt: I have a new client, Marcus Chen, 46, wants to lose body fat and get generally fitter. He's been walking a couple times a week but hasn't done structured training in years. Has high blood pressure, on a beta blocker. Can train 3 days a week, ~45 min, at a commercial gym. Build him a program.
evals.expected_output: Runs ACSM screening: HTN + beta blocker -> flags medical clearance as a BLOCKING gap and notes HR-based targets are unreliable (use RPE/talk test). Asks prioritized MCQ intake for remaining BLOCKING gaps rather than guessing. If it proceeds, uses Base cardio phase + Functional/Movement muscular phase, applies the Ch 13 hypertension FITT table (below VT1, avoid isometrics/inverted, stop-BP limits) as an override, cites pages, and creates clients/marcus_chen_fitness_plan.md and .csv with a traceability chain. Does not prescribe vigorous intensity before clearance.
expectations: Works through an ACSM-style preparticipation screening (regular exercise, known CV/metabolic/renal disease, signs/symptoms, desired intensity)
Flags that medical clearance is needed and treats it as a BLOCKING gap given the hypertension
Notes the beta blocker makes heart-rate-based intensity targets unreliable and recommends RPE or the talk test instead
Applies hypertension-specific guidance as an override: intensity below VT1 / roughly 40-60% HRR, avoid isometric and inverted positions, prolonged cool-down, and stop-exercise BP limits
Asks prioritized multiple-choice intake questions for the remaining blocking gaps instead of fabricating client details
Does not prescribe vigorous-intensity exercise before clearance is obtained
Selects a Base cardio phase and a Functional or Movement muscular-training phase for this deconditioned client
If it produces plan files, they are named clients/marcus_chen_fitness_plan.md and clients/marcus_chen_fitness_plan.csv
Cites specific course pages or tables for the key screening and prescription decisions
Includes an evidence/traceability chain linking a client fact to course guidance to a program decision

evals.expected_output: Loads priya_* plan pair, records the feedback, asks MCQ follow-ups (pain location/severity via the Ch 15 pain scale, onset, history) before changing exercises. Routes to Ch 15 knee section (ITBS pattern for lateral knee pain) + healing-phase contraindication (no pain-causing movement) + post-rehab table. Considers regression (partial-ROM squat) / substitution / load reduction per what the notes support, not an automatic swap. Advises referral if pain persists/worsens (scope). Updates the .md decision log and only changes the .csv if the prescription changed. Does not touch other clients' files.
expectations: Reads the existing priya_nair plan pair (.md and .csv) before proposing changes
Records the knee-pain report in the plan (Client Feedback / Observations and/or Decision Log) rather than silently editing exercises
Asks multiple-choice follow-up questions about the pain (severity/pain-scale, onset, history, other symptoms) before swapping exercises
Routes to the course's knee / musculoskeletal guidance for lateral knee pain and cites it (Ch 15 knee section and/or healing phases / post-rehab table)
Applies the contraindication that pain-causing movement should be avoided, rather than telling her to train through it
Does not do an automatic wholesale exercise swap; presents regression / reduced ROM / load reduction as course-supported options
Advises referral to a physician or physical therapist if the pain persists or worsens, citing scope of practice
Changes the .csv only if the prescription actually changed, and keeps the .md and .csv describing the same program
Does not create or modify any other client's files and keeps the priya_nair filename prefix

Cites pages. Notes medical clearance / working within scope. Flags anything not covered as general knowledge.
expectations: States that a previously active / regular-runner client may generally continue running as tolerated during pregnancy

Lists the key things to avoid: supine position after ~20 weeks, contact sports, fall-risk activities, and extreme heat
Mentions PARmed-X and/or the need for medical clearance and working within scope of practice

Cites a specific course location (Ch 14 pregnancy section and/or Table 14-3)

evals.prompt: New client Dave Ellis, 29, healthy, no conditions, no injuries, trains 4 days a week at a full gym. Been powerlifting 4 years, current 1RMs squat 180 / bench 120 / deadlift 220 kg. Wants to peak all three for a gym meet in about 10 weeks and hit PBs. Build him a program.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the strength-block archetype. Runs ACSM screening (healthy, low risk -> no clearance blocker). Confirms the eligibility gate: experienced (4 yr), states 1RMs, full gym, 4 days -> passes G1-G7 (movement screens still recommended in B3). Uses references/russian-strength-program.md: linear-periodization mesocycle in the Load/Speed stage, V5 or Classic variant, wave on the competition lifts, accessories off the wave. Cites Ch 11 p42-46 periodization, Table 9-12 for the load bands, Ch 10 p69-74 for the 1RM retest with spotting. Times the retest to the meet date. Creates clients/dave_ellis_fitness_plan.md (with the strength-block sections) and .csv. Does not just invent a generic 5x5.
expectations: Identifies this as a max-strength / peaking block and references the Russian Strength Program archetype (references/russian-strength-program.md)
Runs an ACSM-style screening and concludes no medical-clearance blocker for this healthy low-risk client
Works through the eligibility gate (experienced lifter, movement competence, loaded-testing contraindications, equipment, recovery) rather than skipping straight to loads
Selects the Load/Speed muscular-training stage and a linear-periodization mesocycle, citing Ch 11 p42-46
Puts only the core competition lifts on the wave and keeps accessories at a fixed hypertrophy prescription
Plans a 1-RM (or 3-RM) retest timed to the meet date and cites the course's 1-RM assessment / spotting guidance (Ch 10 p69-74)
Maps the loading weeks to the course's goal-based bands (Table 9-12: ~80% hypertrophy/strength band early, >=85% strength/max band late)
If it creates plan files they are clients/dave_ellis_fitness_plan.md and .csv and include the strength-block sections (eligibility gate, wave parameters, retest plan)
The CSV parses cleanly with a consistent column count and integer week values (validate_plan.py reports 0 errors)
Does not fabricate client medical facts; states its assumptions where it proceeds without answers
The prescribed program is recognizably Russian-style: a fixed ~6x2 @ 80% anchor exposure alternating with a volume->intensity progression, not a generic 5x5 / 5-3-1
Wave loads are arithmetically correct: round(target-percent x stated 1-RM) to the nearest 2.5 kg (spot-check several)

evals.prompt: My client Nadia has been training about 3 months, still learning the barbell lifts. She read about the Russian squat program and wants to run it to get strong and lean fast. Can I put her on it?
evals.expected_output: Declines to put her on the archetype now: the >=80% entry load is a FITT-VP 'experienced' value (Table 11-10) and she fails the movement-competence / training-status gates (references/russian-strength-program.md section 2). Does NOT refuse the goal. Offers the scaled entry: a Movement-phase block then a foundational Load/Speed block at 60-70% 1RM, 8-12 reps, 2-4 sets, double progression / 2-for-2, ~5% increments, 8-12 weeks, re-assess, then the Masters variant as a bridge. Records her starting numbers via a sub-maximal rep test (no true 1RM). Handles 'lean fast' honestly and in scope: fat-loss rate is a nutrition/energy-deficit matter, course guidance is ~1-2 lb/wk, general information only, refer to an RD for diet.
expectations: Does not put a 3-month beginner directly on the Russian program / strength-block archetype
Explains why using the course: >=80% 1RM is an experienced-lifter value (Resistance FITT-VP, Table 11-10) and/or movement competence is a prerequisite for the Load/Speed stage
Does not refuse her underlying goal of getting stronger and leaner
Offers a concrete scaled progression: Movement phase then Load/Speed at roughly 60-70% 1RM, 8-12 reps, 2-4 sets, double progression / 2-for-2, with a re-assessment before advancing
Recommends establishing baseline strength with a sub-maximal / rep-max test rather than a true 1-RM
Addresses fat loss within scope: energy deficit drives the rate, course guidance is about 1-2 lb/week, only general non-medical nutrition information, refer to a registered dietitian for a diet
Cites specific course locations for the key claims

evals.prompt: My client's about 5 weeks into the Russian strength block and getting impatient with the fat loss - he wants to crank the deficit hard for the back half to drop the last few kg before we test his maxes. He's asked me to just set his calorie and cardio numbers. What do I tell him?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the back half of the block is the intensification / peak phase - the worst time to deepen a deficit - and recommends holding at roughly maintenance through the peak and the retest so strength and the test aren't compromised (deficit periodisation, russian-strength-program.md section 5; periodization/recovery Ch 11 p42, p47-48). Declines to set specific calorie numbers (meal planning / MNT, outside scope - Ch 1, Ch 6 p5) and refers to an RD. On the cardio ask: the trainer CAN program conditioning, but it should be dosed to recovery headroom and actually pulled BACK in the peak weeks, not cranked up; does not treat 150-250 min/week as a target to chase for a lean trained lifter (that figure is Ch 12 obesity-population guidance). Names the honest trade-off of an aggressive cut into a peak (lost strength, blunted retest, fatigue, poor adherence) and that a bigger deficit is the client's / RD's call. Offers the alternative: finish the block at maintenance, then run a dedicated fat-loss phase afterwards (sequential blocks).
expectations: Identifies that the back half of the block is the intensification / peak phase and that deepening the deficit there is the wrong move
Recommends holding nutrition at roughly maintenance through the peak weeks and the retest to protect strength and the test result
Declines to set specific individualised calorie numbers, names it as outside scope (meal planning / medical nutrition therapy), and refers to a registered dietitian
Addresses the cardio request: the trainer can program conditioning, but it should be dosed to recovery and pulled back in the peak weeks rather than increased
Does not frame 150-250 min/week (or any fixed minute target) as the conditioning goal for this lean, trained client
States the honest trade-offs of an aggressive cut during a peak (lost strength, blunted retest, fatigue, adherence) and that a larger deficit is the client's / RD's decision
Offers the sequential-blocks alternative: finish this block at maintenance, then a dedicated fat-loss phase afterwards
Cites specific course locations (scope Ch 1 / Ch 6 p5; weight management Ch 12 p29-33; periodization / recovery Ch 11 p42, p47-48)

evals.prompt: I've got a client, Sam Reyes, 34, healthy, no injuries, no medical conditions. Trained seriously about 3 years, very comfortable under a heavy bar - recent lifts squat 150kg x 3, bench 100kg x 3, deadlift 190kg x 2. He wants to get noticeably stronger and hit some PBs over the next couple of months, but also drop maybe 4-5kg of fat while he's at it. Trains 4 days a week, full commercial gym. Put a plan together.
evals.expected_output: Uses the strength-block archetype (references/russian-strength-program.md). ACSM screening -> healthy, no clearance blocker. Eligibility gate passes (3 yr experienced, states working loads, full gym, 4 days). Estimates 1RMs from the given rep-maxes (Table 10-25) rather than asking for true 1RMs. Picks a variant (V5 or Classic) and the wave lifts. Handles the concurrent fat loss per section 5: moderate deficit through the accumulation weeks, maintenance through the intensification/peak weeks; adds Zone 1-2 conditioning dosed to recovery (not a fixed minute target) on non-lower-body days and pulled back in the peak; keeps nutrition to general information and refers to an RD (no macro/calorie prescription). Sets a retest method. Creates clients/sam_reyes_fitness_plan.md (with the strength-block sections) and .csv, ideally generated with scripts/russian_block.py.
expectations: Identifies the max-strength / PB goal and uses the Russian Strength Program archetype
Runs an ACSM-style screening and finds no medical-clearance blocker for this healthy client
Works through the eligibility gate and concludes this experienced lifter passes it
Estimates 1RMs from the provided rep-maxes (e.g. via a 1-RM repetition table) instead of requiring true 1-RM tests
Selects a linear-periodization strength block (V5 or Classic variant) in the Load/Speed stage with the core lifts on the wave
Periodises the fat-loss deficit: moderate deficit during the accumulation weeks, maintenance during the intensification / peak weeks
Programs Zone 1-2 conditioning on non-lower-body days, dosed to recovery headroom and reduced in the peak weeks, without treating 150-250 min/week as a fixed target for this lean trained client
Keeps nutrition within scope: general information only, no specific calorie or macro prescription, refers to a registered dietitian
Sets a retest method (true 1-RM/3-RM or a rep-max -> estimated 1-RM)
If it creates plan files they are clients/sam_reyes_fitness_plan.md and .csv and carry the strength-block sections
Cites specific course pages/tables for the load bands, periodization, and weight-management guidance
The wave loads in the CSV are arithmetically correct: each equals round(target-percent x the stated estimated 1-RM) to the nearest 2.5 kg (spot-check several)
